title: Image tag stability & handoff notes
notes:
Purpose:
Quick, personal reference for pinning container images and coordinating handoffs during decoupled deploys. Not a formal runbook — keep it lean and action-oriented for on-call or small deploy windows.

Context:
- We are moving to a two-step deploy: infra rollout (k8s + sidecars) + model/runtime release. Often the failing mode is a mismatch between runtime binary and cache layout. Pinning helps avoid surprises.
- Goal here is to capture the minimum safe steps to release a runtime image while minimizing blast radius.

Goals / acceptance (personal):
- No >2x error-rate spike in first 30m for the canary cohort.
- P95 latency change < 15% for canary.
- Blackbox health checks (kv cache warm success) pass for 90% of canary nodes after 5 minutes.

Quick checklist — pre-rollout (local / before traffic shift):
- Ensure image tag is immutable (use digest) and recorded in the release PR. No floating tags.
- CI: smoke test binary + kv-cache compat test passed in infra PR. Link tests in release PR description.
- Feature flags: ensure feature-flag default = off for new optional behaviors.
- Clients: bump client compatibility header if there are proto/schema changes. Notify SDK owners.
- Telemetry: create a temporary dashboard and alert thresholds for the canary cohort. Save PromQL queries.

Quick checklist — during rollout (incremental):
- Step 1: Canary cohort (internal + 0.5% prod traffic) for 15 mins. Observe errors, p50/p95, token rate, cost anomalies.
- Step 2: If stable, expand to 5% for 30 mins. Watch GC impact, memory growth, swap usage on nodes.
- Step 3: 25% for 20–40 mins. If stable, proceed to full.
- If any threshold tripped, execute backout plan (below).

Backout steps (fast):
- Immediate: flip traffic routing back to previous digest (we have traffic-split config with previous image digest pinned).
- If traffic switch fails: toggle runtime feature flag to safe-path.
- If still degraded: scale down new instance pool and scale up previous pool (manual node group ops).
- Communicate: post status in #deploys and call incident channel if customer impact > 0.5% errors for >10m.

Telemetry to watch (my go-to queries):
- Errors: rate(http_request_errors{route=~"/v1/(generate|chat)"}) by route
- Latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, route) (rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[2m])))
- Auth failures: count_over_time(auth_failure_total[10m])
- Token consumption spike: sum(rate(tokens_generated[1m]))
- Cache misses: rate(kv_cache_miss_total[1m]) / rate(kv_cache_lookup_total[1m])
- Cost proxy: per-token CPU ms * request rate (approx)

Cohort definitions (how I pick groups):
- internal (0.1%): internal accounts, staging mirrored traffic via flag
- small external (0.5%): low-volume customers pre-approved by CS
- wider prod (5–25%): randomized by client-id hashed buckets, exclude tier=enterprise for first 25%

Pinning details (implementation notes):
- Always deploy by image digest in k8s manifest: image: ghcr.io/redwood/runtime@sha256:<digest>
- In the release PR, add a short table mapping: component -> image tag -> digest -> build-id
- Keep a one-line CHANGELOG entry for runtime behavior differences relevant to serving (cache format, kv layout).
- For hotfixes: build new image -> tag as hotfix-YYYYMMDD -> publish digest -> update traffic split; do not reuse previous digest.

Handoff checklist (ops -> on-call / SRE):
- Share link to the pinned digest + release PR in #deploys and #oncall.
- Export the temporary dashboard as a shared link.
- Leave a 30-min shadow window where the engineer who merged stays be reachable.
- Document the exact PromQL/SQL snippets for correlating incidents to release.

Open questions / TODOs (my personal TODOs to finish before finalizing):
- TODO: Confirm whether the load-balancer health-check timeout should be increased for the first 10 minutes post-rollout (Luis to advise).
- TODO: Add a small synthetic test that exercises kv-cache warm path in CI so we catch regressions earlier. (ENG-7123 assigned)
- Question: Should we include a per-client backoff policy in the traffic split service to auto-throttle noisy clients? Pros/cons: reduces human reaction time but hides regressions.

Post-release checks (within 24h):
- Compare daily error budget delta vs previous week for same hour windows.
- Confirm no config drift: image digests in cluster match deploy manifest.
- Spot-check 3 random customers in the 25% cohort for functional correctness (sample requests).

Notes to self (less formal):
- Keep the initial canary tiny. Last time we escalated because we started at 5% and a cache-compat bug burnt ~12% of requests.
- If rolling out near EU morning, move windows to avoid peak APAC traffic.
- Communicate early to product owners — better to be conservative and get a small delay than a rushed rollback.

Links / bookmarks:
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234
- Release playbook (canonical): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/987654321/Release+Playbook
- JIRA for cache warm CI: ENG-7123

End of scratchpad. Keep this short and prune after we have a stable cadence.
